title: Fear and hope
hook: the believer flies with two wings, fear and hope

segments.voice: Yesterday, mahabbah, love of Allah, and your line: love follows. Did your one quiet extra thing get done, and did you manage not to mention it? Day one thousand two hundred seventy-nine.

A bird with one wing doesn't fly. It goes in circles on the ground. Ibn al-Qayyim, a later scholar who wrote about the stations of the path, used a bird to picture the heart on its way to Allah. Love, yesterday's station, is the head. And the two wings are fear and hope. Readers draw out the lesson: lose the wing of fear, and the bird tips into carelessness. Lose the wing of hope, and it tips into despair. Either way, it doesn't get off the ground. Today, the pair that has to beat together.
screen: `ONE WING GOES IN CIRCLES.` → `LOVE IS THE HEAD.` → `FEAR AND HOPE ARE THE WINGS.`

segments.voice: In Arabic the pair is khawf and raja, fear and hope, and the Qur'an puts them side by side. Describing the believers at night, it says, in Pickthall's translation, that they "forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope." Not fear, then hope. Both, in the same prayer. What does each wing do? Fear, here, isn't panic. It's taking seriously that your choices matter, that a reckoning is real, the evening ledger from a few days ago. It keeps a person honest. Hope is trusting that Allah's mercy is bigger than your mistakes. The Qur'an says it straight out, in Pickthall's words: "Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins." Hope keeps a person from giving up. Now the scene that holds them both. In the collection of al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ visits a young man who is dying, and asks him how he finds himself. The young man answers: I hope in Allah, and I fear my sins. The Prophet says that whenever these two come together in a servant's heart at a moment like that, Allah gives him what he hopes for and keeps him safe from what he fears. Notice he didn't tell the young man to drop either one. He blessed the pair. So the question for a heart isn't fear or hope. It's whether both wings are still moving, and whether one has quietly stopped.
screen: `KHAWF AND RAJA, SIDE BY SIDE.` · `FEAR KEEPS YOU HONEST.` · `HOPE KEEPS YOU GOING.` · `A YOUNG MAN, HOLDING BOTH.`

segments.voice: The practice: balance one worry with one hope. Settle, and breathe. Bring up one thing you're worried about in yourself. Not the world, yourself. A habit, a temper, a thing you keep putting off. Let that be the wing of fear: honest, not frantic. Now find the other wing. One real reason for hope about that same thing. A time you did better. Someone who forgave you. If you pray, the line: despair not of the mercy of Allah. Hold the worry and the hope side by side, and breathe as if both wings were moving together. The bell holds the time.
Fear and hope. Khawf and raja: taking your choices seriously, and trusting that mercy is bigger than your mistakes, held together like two wings. Today's word.
Your line: two wings. Today, when you catch yourself leaning hard on one, careless or discouraged, reach for the other. Tomorrow, sincerity of intention. Day one thousand two hundred seventy-nine.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers describe fear of Allah and hope in His mercy as two things a believer holds together, and some families at a deathbed speak of Allah's mercy so that hope is strong at the end.

myth: the Qur'an asks for fear first, then later for hope
it describes believers who cry to their Lord "in fear and hope," both at once.
the Prophet told the dying young man to stop fearing
he blessed the pair: Allah gives what such a heart hopes for and keeps it safe from what it fears.
the bird picture of love, fear and hope comes from Ibn al-Qayyim
love is the head; fear and hope are the two wings.

fork.setup: the Prophet ﷺ visits a young man who is dying and asks how he finds himself. what does the young man say?
options: I'm afraid of my sins, and nothing else.
I hope in Allah, and I fear my sins.
fork.reveal: he holds both. the Prophet says that when the two meet in a heart at such a moment, Allah gives what it hopes and keeps it safe from what it fears.

trapdoor: what you thought: religion is either about fear or about comfort.
what it means: two wings, beating together. fear keeps you honest, hope keeps you going.
what a scholar hears: 32:16, 'in fear and hope', the dying young man in al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn al-Qayyim's bird with love for its head.
